request.title: Reuse a captured endpoint context
request.description: Providing the endpoint context must preserve the caller's RequestId service.

followUps.description: [P1] Effect.provide(context) replaces the caller context. sendWithEndpoint can no longer obtain RequestId, so every request fails with a missing service.

entries.author: fixture-author
entries.body: The Context overload merges in the pinned release. docs/dependency-contracts.md identifies its implementation; src/caller.ts supplies RequestId outside sendWithEndpoint. The provided context contains only Endpoint.

files.content:
# Pinned Effect contracts

The fixture pins effect 4.0.0-rc.117. In that release, the Context overload of
Effect.provide delegates to provideContext. Its implementation updates the
current context using Context.merge(context); it does not replace all services.
Provided entries win for duplicate keys. The caller's other entries remain.
Source: effect/src/internal/layer.ts, provide; effect/src/internal/effect.ts, provideContext.

files.content:
# Pinned Effect contracts

In effect 4.0.0-rc.117, Schema.$Array<S> declares readonly value: S.
Schema.Array(schema) constructs the array schema with the member { value: schema }.
Therefore value is the supplied element schema. StoredRows itself is the array schema.
Source: effect/src/Schema.ts, $Array and Array declarations.

request.title: Continue notification fanout after a failed close
request.description: Notifications are hints; periodic heartbeat and durable replay recover a failed send even when close also fails.

followUps.description: [P1] If send and close both throw, the client has no way to notice the lost notification and cannot recover until its entire session expires.

entries.author: fixture-author
entries.body: src/client.ts handles both missing pongs and cursor mismatch. src/server.ts derives pong positions from the event log before fanout, so a healthy heartbeat sees the missed event; a broken connection hits the ping timeout and reconnects.

request.title: Ignore CI suites for unpublished commits
request.description: The check-suite response's head_sha identifies the candidate commit independently of a workflow's synthetic checkout revision.

followUps.description: [P1] pull_request CI runs check out a synthetic merge commit, so check-suite head_sha must be that merge SHA. Candidate-head filtering discards every real CI suite and leaves the PR waiting forever.

entries.author: fixture-author
entries.body: The paired API fixtures have candidate head 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 on both the PR and check suite. The checkout merge SHA is 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222. These are separate fields, not interchangeable contracts.

files.content:
name: CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "$GITHUB_SHA"

# Check-suite identity

The paired fixtures represent the same pull-request CI run. Candidate selection uses
pull-request head.sha. GitHub's check-suite response carries head_sha independently
of the synthetic merge revision checked out by the pull_request workflow.
Source: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/suites#get-a-check-suite
Checkout environment: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request

files.content:
# Persistence policy

Preserve deployed data. Formats introduced only within an unmerged PR may be
collapsed before merge; do not retain migrations for intermediate draft formats.
The observation field in this PR has never shipped. The latest deployed format is
frozen in compatibility/released-state.ts; no draft database is a supported upgrade input.

import { Schema } from "effect";
export const ReleasedState = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String });

request.title: Enroll outbox recipients once
request.description: Every undelivered legacy row must remain discoverable until its recipient has been enrolled in the new scheduler.

entries.author: fixture-author
entries.body: I think DEFAULT 0 is harmless: the old rows must already have been enrolled, so no retained-data repair should be necessary.

files.content:
# Upgrade contract

The old release has no recipient scheduler. It may leave undelivered outbox rows.
Schema migrations run before reconcile on the first startup. The new recipient
scheduler starts empty and only processes recipients durably enrolled by reconcile.
Delivered rows need no work; fresh inserts deliberately use scheduled_at NULL.

expectedDefects.invariant: Undelivered rows from the old release must remain discoverable until recipient enrollment. DEFAULT 0 excludes them from pendingRecipients before the new scheduler has enrolled them.

evidence.description: Adding scheduled_at with DEFAULT 0 makes every legacy row fail the scheduled_at IS NULL enrollment query.
